transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording id: ff-20250218-78642
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Noah (Redwood CSM), Tim (Timberlane Head of Platform), Priya (Security Lead), Elena (Data Engineer), Marcus (SRE)

Summary:
Quick weekly pilot sync focused on security/compliance open items. Customer wants clarity on audit logging, retention windows, SSO/SCIM flows for provisioning, and how Redwood stores tokenized inputs during the pilot. Redwood to provide SOC 2 artifacts, sample audit log export, and schedule an infra deep-dive. Several minor transcription errors present.

[00:00] Samir: hey everybody, thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight, main ask today is to lock down the security checklist and the next steps for the pilot.
[00:18] Tim: cool, thanks Samir. we ran the small batch of inference yesterday and results look fine; before we expand we need to make sure audit logs and retention meet our compliance team.
[00:30] Priya: yeah hi, i'm priya. key things are SOC 2 evidence, SSO/SAML integration for our engineers, and a clear retention/deletion story — especially for EU PII.
[00:45] Maya: great hi priya, im maya from Redwood, i'm the SE on the account. quick overview, Redwood hosted pilot by default keeps ephemeral request data for 30 days for debugging unless configured; we have options for shorter retention, and deletion APIs.
[01:10] Marcus: when you say ephemeral, is that full request body or only metadata/trace? we need to know exactly what persists.
[01:25] Maya: good question. default debug retention includes full request payload for the trial window — but it's encrypted at rest with customer managed KMS optionality. for production we recommend disabling payload retention and only keep structured audit logs.
[01:45] Elena: can you share the schema for audit logs? we need to map it into our SIEM (we use Splunk).
[02:00] Samir: yes, we'll share a sample export — maya will attach a CSV + JSON schema. note there are some field name differences in the current pilot export, the transcript tool occasionally mashes names (e.g., "KV cache" is sometimes transcribed odd).
[02:20] Tim: what's the retention configuration surface? is it per-route, per-model, or global?
[02:28] Maya: retention is configurable per-tenant and per-route; admin console lets you set default retention windows and overrides. for the pilot you can set per-model retention to meet compliance.
[02:42] Priya: do you have a SLA for purge? like once we set deletion, how fast is data actually purged?
[02:50] Maya: hard delete runs within 24 hours for most object types, and audit logs are rotated to archival thereafter based on policy. for full air-gapped/private deployments, purge behavior is controlled entirely on your side.
[03:05] Marcus: we will need proof of the purge, maybe a checksum or a log entry that confirms deletion for auditors.
[03:15] Samir: we can provide a deletion confirmation event in the audit log; we'll pull that into the sample export.
[03:25] Tim: SSO — we need SAML with Okta and SCIM provisioning so engineers and contractors sync automatically. is SCIM supported in the pilot?
[03:40] Maya: yes, SCIM is supported; you can use Okta SCIM connector to provision groups and assign roles. SCIM provisioning can be enabled in the pilot with a couple caveats around group mapping.
[04:00] Priya: can we lock down role-based access control? we don't want broad admin rights for contractors.
[04:08] Maya: RBAC is role-based with admin, developer, auditor roles; SCIM group-to-role mapping lets you limit privileges. we'll send the RBAC mapping doc.
[04:22] Elena: audit log format again — do you include the API key/consumer id and route, but not request content if we disable payload retention?
[04:33] Maya: correct. audit logs include request metadata: consumer id, route, model, timestamps, response size, latency, and if enabled, a request hash. payloads are omitted if you disable retention.
[04:50] Priya: what's the encryption story — is it envelope encryption with CMKs?
[04:56] Samir: we support platform-managed encryption by default, and customer-managed keys via KMS for hosted Dedicated customers. for private deployments you can use your own HSM.
[05:12] Tim: SOC 2 — do you publish the full report or a summary? auditors usually want the full attestations.
[05:20] Samir: we can share the SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA; i'll attach the PDF and a one-pager of control mappings to the pilot checklist.
[05:35] Priya: good. on logging frequency — we need streaming log delivery into our S3/Splunk or maybe a syslog endpoint. do you support push/forwarders?
[05:48] Maya: we support delivery to S3, to SIEM via Kinesis or direct ingestion, and a webhook interface for streaming audit events. for the pilot we can set up a periodic export to your S3 bucket.
[06:05] Marcus: any cost for log exports? we need to estimate egress to S3.
[06:12] Samir: exports are included but heavy retention/long-term storage has separate pricing; we'll include a rough estimate in the follow-up.
[06:28] Tim: on the technical side, we saw some latency spikes in the evening. not a compliance issue but thought you'd want to know.
[06:35] Maya: thanks, we'll correlate with the tokenization and KV-cache behavior; sometimes batching settings cause spikes. we'll push a tuning suggestion in the follow-up.
[06:52] Elena: deletion API — is there a way to request deletion for a specific user or dataset?
[06:59] Maya: yes, we have a deletion API that accepts filters (user id, dataset id, timestamp range) and returns a job id which can be polled until completion.
[07:15] Priya: will that job id be visible in the audit log? auditors need traceability.
[07:22] Maya: yes, deletion job lifecycle events appear as audit events with job id, owner, start/finish times, and affected object counts.
[07:35] Tim: happy to see that. any concerns about data residency? we have some EU customers so logs and any persisted PII need to live in the EU region.
[07:45] Samir: region pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private; for hosted we can pin region for data storage — we'll confirm exact region support for the EU cluster.
[07:58] Marcus: can you produce a list of the physical locations where backups are stored? should be part of the audit pack.
[08:05] Samir: yes, we'll include high-level geographic backup info in the security pack (not detailed physical addresses).
[08:18] Priya: one more question — do you have log masking for PII in transit? we want to obfuscate or hash specific fields automatically.
[08:28] Maya: we have built-in field scrubbers that can hash or redact fields based on regex rules; you can apply them per-route. we'll include examples for common PII patterns.
[08:45] Elena: will scrubbers affect model quality? we need to know if we remove llm inputs it could impact outputs.
[08:53] Maya: yes if you remove core prompt text you may affect results — recommend keeping a hashed token to allow debugging while preserving privacy.
[09:10] Tim: procurement loop — do you have a standard DPPA/processing addendum? procurement may need that soon.
[09:18] Samir: yes, we have a Data Processing Addendum and standard security appendix; legal can share it once we engage with procurement.
[09:30] Priya: any red flags or gaps for SOC 2 controls? we need to understand the control ownership map between Redwood and Timberlane.
[09:40] Samir: we'll deliver a control matrix mapping responsibilities for access control, data handling, incident response.
[09:48] Marcus: incident response — how fast are you notifying customers? what's the SLA for breach notification?
[09:56] Maya: we have an incident response playbook; notification timelines are part of the SLA — typically within 72 hours for confirmed incidents; for enterprise customers we can negotiate shorter windows.
[10:12] Tim: ok. let's talk briefly about the pilot timeline — we wanted a gradual expansion pending these security checks. assume an extra week if we need to wait for SOC2 docs?
[10:25] Samir: that sounds reasonable. we'll aim to get docs out within 48 hours and the infra deep dive next week.
[10:35] Elena: can you also include an example of the audit log ingestion config for Splunk? a sample props/transforms would be helpful.
[10:42] Maya: yes, we'll include Splunk example and a sample S3 lifecycle policy.
[10:55] Tim: anything else on routing/fallback? we had a question about deterministic fallbacks and model version pinning in case of degradation.
[11:03] Maya: Redwood supports model pinning and fallback policies; we'll share the route policy docs.
[11:15] Samir: wrap-up then: action items and next steps as discussed.
[11:20] Priya: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[11:25] Tim: thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround.

End of meeting.

Notes: transcript contains small mis-transcriptions (product names and acronyms) — audience should rely on attached artifacts for exact field names. Follow-up attachments to include: SOC2 PDF (NDA), audit log sample CSV + JSON schema, RBAC mapping doc, Splunk ingest example, deletion API docs, SSO/SCIM quickstart and Okta mapping notes.
